summary:
Ashad, the Lone Cyberman is an artifact engine. Casualty 2 on the first nonlegendary artifact spell each turn turns it into a token copy. This review re-verifies the retrospective attestation (Twinning Staff, Solemn and Ichor Wellspring copies, flash timing, 'another creature').

Rules surprises:
- Casualty copies aren't 'created' tokens, so Worldwalker Helm adds no Map.
- Biotransference makes your creatures artifacts, so your own Delete and Their Name Is Death spare them.

No list errors.

interactions.title: Casualty 2 on your first nonlegendary artifact spell
interactions.ruling: The first nonlegendary artifact spell you cast each turn has casualty 2. Sacrificing a creature with power 2 or greater as you cast it copies the spell. The copy of a permanent spell resolves into a token. Only the *first* nonlegendary artifact spell each turn qualifies. Legendary artifacts (The Cyber-Controller, Mox Opal, Iron Man) neither get casualty nor use up the 'first'. Artifact lands are played, not cast.
interactions.short: First nonlegendary artifact spell each turn: sacrifice power 2+ to copy it into a token.

oracle.quote: The first nonlegendary artifact spell you cast each turn has casualty 2.

rulings.quote: You may sacrifice only one creature to pay a spell's casualty cost, and you copy the spell only once.
The copy of the spell is created on the stack, so it's not "cast." Abilities that trigger when a player casts a spell won't trigger.

source.quote: the copied permanent spell is not cast and becomes a token as it resolves.

interactions.title: The +1/+1 trigger needs *another* creature sacrificed
interactions.ruling: Ashad gets a +1/+1 counter whenever you sacrifice another creature: casualty payments, Ashnod's Altar, Phyrexian Altar, Krark-Clan Ironworks on an artifact creature. Sacrificing Ashad itself doesn't count.

oracle.quote: Whenever you sacrifice another creature, put a +1/+1 counter on Ashad.

source.quote: Ashad's +1/+1 trigger is for sacrificing **another** creature

interactions.title: Casualty tokens aren't 'created': no Worldwalker Helm Map
interactions.ruling:
A copy of a permanent spell becomes a token as it resolves but isn't 'created' for replacement effects or triggers that refer to creating tokens. Worldwalker Helm adds no Map for Ashad's copy.

Enter triggers still work: the token Solemn Simulacrum fetches a land, the token Ichor Wellspring draws, and Simulacrum Synthesizer sees an artifact with MV 3 or more enter, because the copy keeps the mana cost.
interactions.short: Casualty copies enter as tokens but aren't 'created': enter triggers work, Helm's Map doesn't.

oracle.quote: If you would create one or more artifact tokens, instead create those tokens plus an additional Map token.

source.quote: A copied `Solemn Simulacrum` spell resolves as its own token permanent and supplies its own enter-the-battlefield trigger.

interactions.title: Twinning Staff applies to artifact spell copies
interactions.ruling: Twinning Staff's replacement covers copying any spell, so an Ashad casualty copy becomes two copies (two tokens). Staff's {7} activated ability is the part limited to instants and sorceries.

oracle.quote: If you would copy a spell one or more times, instead copy it that many times plus an additional time.

source.quote: That replacement effect is not limited to instants and sorceries; therefore it applies to Ashad copying a nonlegendary artifact permanent spell.

interactions.title: Urza + Worldwalker Helm + Artificer Class
interactions.ruling:
Commander Spellbook (66-457-5491, cached) lists this as infinite artifact tokens and blue mana. Its line, with Artificer Class at level 3:
1. At your end step, the Class makes a token copy of Worldwalker Helm plus a Map.
2. Urza taps a Helm and a Map for {U}{U}.
3. A Helm token copies itself ({1}{U}, {T}), creating another Helm token plus a Map *for each Helm you control*.
4. Urza taps two Maps for {U}{U}. Repeat from step 3.

Urza's {5} then exiles and plays the library.
interactions.short: Spellbook infinite: Helm tokens copy themselves with Urza paying via the tokens and Maps.

oracle.quote: {1}{U}, {T}: Create a token that's a copy of target artifact token you control.
Tap an untapped artifact you control: Add {U}.
At the beginning of your end step, create a token that's a copy of target artifact you control.

rulings.quote: Worldwaker Helm's first ability applies to all kinds of artifact tokens that its controller creates, not just Map tokens.

spellbook.quote: Activate a Worldwalker Helm by paying {1}{U} and tapping it, creating a token copy of the Worldwalker Helm token plus a Map token for each Worldwalker Helm you control.

interactions.title: Ashad's casualty copy of Worldwalker Helm as the starting token
interactions.ruling: Our derivation, not a Spellbook line. Casting Worldwalker Helm as your first nonlegendary artifact spell with casualty gives a token Helm. It isn't 'created', so no Map, but it's an artifact token that Helm's ability can target. With Urza, tap the nontoken Helm and another artifact for {U}{U}, then activate the token Helm. It copies itself and gets two Maps (two Helms on the battlefield), and steps 3–4 of the Spellbook line follow without Artificer Class.
interactions.uncertainty: Reconstructed from Oracle text and CR 111.13; not a Commander Spellbook variant. It needs a second untapped artifact for the first {U}{U}.

oracle.quote: The first nonlegendary artifact spell you cast each turn has casualty 2.

interactions.title: Biotransference makes creature spells artifact spells
interactions.ruling:
Biotransference makes your creature spells, your creatures and your creature cards in other zones artifacts too.
- Nonlegendary creature spells (Mayhem Devil, Marionette Master, Pitiless Plunderer) become eligible for Ashad's casualty, artifact cost reducers and Jhoira.
- Delete and Their Name Is Death hit only nonartifact creatures, so they spare your board.

The effect is a layer 4 type change. Replacement effects that modify artifacts entering apply after it.
interactions.short: Biotransference: your creatures become artifacts, so they get casualty and survive Delete and Their Name Is Death.

oracle.quote: Creatures you control are artifacts in addition to their other types. The same is true for creature spells you control and creature cards you own that aren't on the battlefield.
Delete deals X damage to each nonartifact creature and each player.

rulings.quote: Replacement effects that modify artifacts as they enter the battlefield will apply after you apply Biotransference's effect.

interactions.title: Iron Man copies legendary artifacts as nonlegendary
interactions.ruling: Iron Man's once-per-turn copy works on any artifact spell, including legendary ones (the copy isn't legendary). It covers The Cyber-Controller, which Ashad can't copy; the copy keeps X. On a nonlegendary spell, Ashad's casualty copy and Iron Man's copy stack. Twinning Staff adds one to each copy event.

oracle.quote: Whenever you cast an artifact spell, you may copy it, except the copy isn't legendary. Do this only once each turn.

interactions.title: Flash artifacts reuse 'first each turn' on other turns
interactions.ruling: Ashad's casualty resets every turn, not just yours. With Shimmer Myr, artifact spells can be cast at instant speed, so you can cast a nonlegendary artifact with casualty on each opponent's turn. Artifact lands aren't affected (they're played).

oracle.quote: You may cast artifact spells as though they had flash.

rulings.quote: Shimmer Myr has no effect on artifact lands because they aren't cast as spells.

source.quote: Flash-granting artifact infrastructure can exploit Ashad's “first ... each turn” wording on other players' turns

interactions.title: Sacrifice and artifact-death drains
interactions.ruling:
- **Artifact leaves the battlefield:** artifact tokens are put into the graveyard before ceasing to exist, so Disciple of the Vault and Marionette Master trigger for each sacrificed Treasure, Servo or casualty token.
- **Any sacrifice:** Mayhem Devil triggers on each one, including the casualty payment and opponents' sacrifices.
- **Artifacts entering:** Ingenious Artillerist and Reckless Fireweaver trigger on each artifact that enters, tokens from casualty included.

oracle.quote: Whenever an artifact is put into a graveyard from the battlefield, you may have target opponent lose 1 life.
Whenever a player sacrifices a permanent, this creature deals 1 damage to any target.

interactions.title: Myriad: Cybermen Squadron and Auton Soldier
interactions.ruling: Cybermen Squadron gives nonlegendary artifact creatures myriad, so Ashad (legendary) doesn't get it. Myriad tokens enter attacking but weren't declared as attackers, so 'whenever attacks' abilities don't trigger for them. The tokens are exiled at end of combat. With only one opponent left, myriad makes nothing.

rulings.quote: Although the tokens enter the battlefield attacking, they were never declared as attackers.
If the defending player is your only opponent, no tokens are put onto the battlefield.

interactions.title: Esoteric Duplicator rebuys sacrificed artifacts
interactions.ruling: Whenever you sacrifice Duplicator or another artifact (artifact creatures to an altar or casualty, Treasures, KCI fodder), you may pay {2} for an end-step token copy. The copy copies the printed card (or the original token characteristics) without counters. Its enter triggers work.

rulings.quote: If the copied artifact was a token, the token that’s created copies the original characteristics of that token as stated by the effect that created that token.

interactions.title: Portal to Phyrexia with casualty
interactions.ruling: Portal to Phyrexia is a nonlegendary artifact spell. A casualty copy resolves into a token Portal with its own enter trigger, so each opponent sacrifices three creatures twice, and you get two upkeep reanimation triggers.

oracle.quote: When this artifact enters, each opponent sacrifices three creatures of their choice.

interactions.title: Commander tax and Ashad's artifact type
interactions.ruling: Ashad is a four-mana legendary artifact creature ({1}{U}{B}{R}, then 6, 8). As a legendary it doesn't trigger its own casualty, and Cybermen Squadron doesn't give it myriad. If Ashad goes to the graveyard you may move it to the command zone. If you leave it there, Academy Ruins can put it on top of the library because it's an artifact card.

oracle.quote: {1}{U}, {T}: Put target artifact card from your graveyard on top of your library.
